title: Research Publication: Multidepth Soil Sensor System for Monitoring Root Zone Stability in Oil Palm Plantations
excerpt: Yogyakarta, June 15, 2026 – Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada has produced another research publication in the prestigious international journal Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Q1) published by Elsevier. This research develops a multidepth soil monitoring system to measure soil moisture and soil temperature conditions…
body:
**Yogyakarta, June 15, 2026** – **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** has produced another research publication in the prestigious international journal **Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Q1)** published by **Elsevier**. This research develops a **multidepth soil monitoring system** to measure **soil moisture** and **soil temperature** conditions on tropical oil palm plantations, particularly on **Spodosol** land that has a hardpan layer.

Oil palm plantations on tropical land often face challenges related to water availability in the root zone. On Spodosol land, the presence of a hardpan layer can limit water and plant root movement. This condition makes changes in soil water and temperature not always the same at each depth. Therefore, **soil monitoring at a single depth alone is often insufficient** to accurately describe the conditions in the root zone.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/794-1-image-22-773x1030.webp)

The research titled **"Multidepth soil sensing with an embedded hydrothermal stress index captures stratified stability in hardpan-limited tropical spodosol oil palm systems"** was conducted by **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Kevin Ezekiel Manik, Fadel Arya Pradana, Lilik Sutiarso, and Takashi Okayasu**. The article has been published in **Computers and Electronics in Agriculture Volume 251 Year 2026** with article number **112026**.

The developed system uses soil sensors installed at **three depths**, namely **0–10 cm, 10–42 cm, and 42–68 cm**. These three layers are used to represent surface soil conditions, middle layer, and deeper layer above the hardpan. The sensors periodically measure soil moisture and soil temperature, then transmit data through a system based on **ESP32 microcontroller, RS485 communication, GSM/GPRS module**, and supported by **solar panels** to operate independently in the field.

Simply put, this research does not just measure whether soil is wet or dry, but also examines how water and temperature conditions change at each soil depth. This information is then processed into an index called the **Hydrothermal Root Zone Stress Index (HRZSI)**. This index is used to describe the stability level of the root zone based on a combination of **soil moisture** and **soil temperature** data from multiple depths.

The research was conducted at a **rainfed oil palm plantation in Central Kalimantan**. Data were collected continuously, then filtered and summarized into **227 daily data points**. The developed sensor system was also validated using comparison methods, and the results showed very good performance with an **R² value of 0.987, RMSE of 1.00%, and MAPE of 2.38%**.

The research findings show that soil conditions at each depth have different characteristics. The surface layer responds more quickly to rainfall and weather changes, while deeper layers show more seasonal water storage and depletion patterns. This proves that **monitoring at a single depth alone is insufficient** to understand water conditions in the root zone of oil palm on Spodosol land.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/794-2-image-23-1030x613.webp)

Through the **HRZSI**, the observation period can be grouped into three conditions: **Stable, Transitional, and Unstable**. Out of **227 observation days**, **161 days or 70.93%** fall into the **Stable** category, **46 days or 20.26%** fall into the **Transitional** category, and **20 days or 8.81%** fall into the **Unstable** category. This result shows that the system is capable of providing a more measurable picture of soil water and temperature stability in the root zone.

This research also demonstrates that monitoring based solely on surface soil is less able to represent the overall stability of the root zone. In contrast, a combination of data from multiple depths and soil temperature information provides a stronger and more accurate picture of actual conditions. Thus, this system can serve as a foundation for developing **more precise soil monitoring for oil palm plantations**.

## **Collaboration and Support:**

This research was carried out through collaboration between **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada**, and the **Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Agriculture, Kyushu University, Japan**. The research also received field implementation support from **Wilmar International Plantation, Central Kalimantan Region, Indonesia**.

This collaboration brings together expertise in **precision agriculture, multidepth soil sensors, embedded systems, hydrothermal monitoring, data analysis**, and **oil palm plantation management on tropical land**. Through this collaboration, the research not only focuses on sensor system development but is also directed to address actual needs in monitoring root zone conditions on Spodosol land that has physical soil limitations.

This research received funding support from **Universitas Gadjah Mada through Academic Excellence C Scheme 2025 No. 5719/UN1.P2/Dit-Lit/PT.01.03/2025**. The research team also expresses appreciation to the **Working Group Food Security (WG.FS 1.2) Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming, Inter-University Excellence Center (PUAPT) Universitas Gadjah Mada**, for research facility support, and to **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** for technical and institutional support. Appreciation is also extended to **Nada Berliana Kusumawati, Iqbal Maulana Haryadi, Muhdan Syarovy, Suwardi, Sukarman, and Septa Primananda** for technical assistance in system development, field equipment installation, and data acquisition.

## **Benefits and Impact:**

This research makes an important contribution to the development of **soil monitoring systems on tropical oil palm plantations**. With multidepth monitoring, plantation managers can obtain more complete information regarding root zone conditions, not just surface soil conditions. This information can help support decision-making related to **irrigation, drainage, water management, and plant stress mitigation**.

This system also has the potential to help plantation managers identify periods when the root zone is in **stable, transitional, or unstable** conditions. With this information, field actions can be taken more timely and data-driven. This approach is especially important on land with hardpan layers, since surface water conditions do not necessarily represent water conditions in deeper soil layers.

From the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** perspective, this research supports **SDG 2: Zero Hunger** as it contributes to technology development in support of agricultural system productivity and sustainability. This research also aligns with **SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation** through the potential for more efficient water management on plantation systems. Furthermore, the development of **multidepth sensors, embedded systems, and hydrothermal indices** supports **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure** through smart agriculture technology innovation. In the long term, this technology also contributes to **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production** and **SDG 13: Climate Action**, as it can help promote more adaptive, efficient, and sustainable water and soil resource management.

Going forward, this system has the potential to be further developed through validation across various **soil types, hardpan depths, drainage conditions, groundwater levels, canopy structures**, and **different plantation management zones**. Further integration with **Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, monitoring dashboards, early warning systems, and decision-making models** can strengthen the role of this technology in supporting water management and hydrothermal stress monitoring on tropical oil palm plantations.

**The complete research publication can be accessed through the following DOI link:** [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2026.112026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2026.112026)

**Contact:** **Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc.** **ardan.w@ugm.ac.id**

original.title: Publikasi Penelitian: Sistem Sensor Tanah Multikedalaman untuk Memantau Stabilitas Zona Perakaran Kelapa Sawit

original.body:
**Yogyakarta, 15 Juni 2026** – **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** kembali menghasilkan publikasi penelitian di jurnal internasional bereputasi **Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Q1)** yang diterbitkan oleh **Elsevier**. Penelitian ini mengembangkan **sistem pemantauan tanah multikedalaman** untuk membaca kondisi **lengas tanah** dan **suhu tanah** pada perkebunan kelapa sawit tropis, khususnya pada lahan **Spodosol** yang memiliki lapisan keras atau **hardpan**.

Perkebunan kelapa sawit di lahan tropis sering menghadapi tantangan terkait ketersediaan air di zona perakaran. Pada lahan Spodosol, keberadaan lapisan hardpan dapat membatasi pergerakan air dan akar tanaman. Kondisi ini membuat perubahan air dan suhu tanah tidak selalu sama pada setiap kedalaman. Oleh karena itu, **pemantauan tanah pada satu kedalaman saja sering kali belum cukup** untuk menggambarkan kondisi sebenarnya di zona perakaran.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/794-1-image-22-773x1030.webp)

Penelitian yang berjudul **“Multidepth soil sensing with an embedded hydrothermal stress index captures stratified stability in hardpan-limited tropical spodosol oil palm systems”** ini dilakukan oleh **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Kevin Ezekiel Manik, Fadel Arya Pradana, Lilik Sutiarso, dan Takashi Okayasu**. Artikel ini telah dipublikasikan dalam **Computers and Electronics in Agriculture Volume 251 Tahun 2026** dengan nomor artikel **112026**.

Sistem yang dikembangkan menggunakan sensor tanah yang dipasang pada **tiga kedalaman**, yaitu **0–10 cm, 10–42 cm, dan 42–68 cm**. Ketiga lapisan ini digunakan untuk merepresentasikan kondisi tanah permukaan, lapisan tengah, dan lapisan lebih dalam yang berada di atas hardpan. Sensor tersebut membaca lengas tanah dan suhu tanah secara berkala, kemudian data dikirimkan melalui sistem berbasis **mikrokontroler ESP32, komunikasi RS485, modul GSM/GPRS**, serta didukung oleh **panel surya** agar dapat bekerja secara mandiri di lapangan.

Secara sederhana, penelitian ini tidak hanya membaca apakah tanah basah atau kering, tetapi juga melihat bagaimana kondisi air dan suhu berubah pada setiap kedalaman tanah. Informasi ini kemudian diolah menjadi indeks yang disebut **Hydrothermal Root Zone Stress Index (HRZSI)**. Indeks ini digunakan untuk menggambarkan tingkat stabilitas zona perakaran berdasarkan kombinasi data **lengas tanah** dan **suhu tanah** dari beberapa kedalaman.

Penelitian dilakukan di **perkebunan kelapa sawit tadah hujan di Kalimantan Tengah**. Data dikumpulkan secara kontinu, kemudian disaring dan diringkas menjadi **227 data harian**. Sistem sensor yang dikembangkan juga divalidasi menggunakan metode pembanding, dan hasilnya menunjukkan performa yang sangat baik dengan nilai **R² sebesar 0,987, RMSE sebesar 1,00%, dan MAPE sebesar 2,38%**.

Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kondisi tanah pada setiap kedalaman memiliki karakter yang berbeda. Lapisan permukaan lebih cepat merespons perubahan hujan dan cuaca, sedangkan lapisan yang lebih dalam menunjukkan pola penyimpanan dan penurunan air yang lebih musiman. Hal ini membuktikan bahwa **pemantauan satu kedalaman saja belum cukup** untuk memahami kondisi air di zona perakaran kelapa sawit pada lahan Spodosol.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/794-2-image-23-1030x613.webp)

Melalui **HRZSI**, periode pengamatan dapat dikelompokkan menjadi tiga kondisi, yaitu **Stable, Transitional, dan Unstable**. Dari **227 hari pengamatan**, sebanyak **161 hari atau 70,93%** termasuk kategori **Stable**, **46 hari atau 20,26%** termasuk kategori **Transitional**, dan **20 hari atau 8,81%** termasuk kategori **Unstable**. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu memberikan gambaran yang lebih terukur mengenai stabilitas kondisi air dan suhu tanah pada zona perakaran.

Penelitian ini juga menunjukkan bahwa pemantauan berbasis tanah permukaan saja kurang mampu mewakili stabilitas keseluruhan zona perakaran. Sebaliknya, kombinasi data dari beberapa kedalaman serta informasi suhu tanah memberikan gambaran yang lebih kuat dan lebih mendekati kondisi aktual. Dengan demikian, sistem ini dapat menjadi dasar pengembangan **pemantauan tanah yang lebih presisi untuk perkebunan kelapa sawit**.

## **Kolaborasi dan Dukungan:**

Penelitian ini terlaksana melalui kolaborasi antara **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada**, dengan **Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Agriculture, Kyushu University, Jepang**. Penelitian ini juga mendapatkan dukungan implementasi lapangan dari **Wilmar International Plantation, Region Kalimantan Tengah, Indonesia**.

Kolaborasi ini mempertemukan keahlian dalam bidang **pertanian presisi, sensor tanah multikedalaman, sistem tertanam, pemantauan hidrotermal, analisis data**, serta **pengelolaan perkebunan kelapa sawit pada lahan tropis**. Melalui kolaborasi tersebut, penelitian ini tidak hanya berfokus pada pengembangan sistem sensor, tetapi juga diarahkan untuk menjawab kebutuhan nyata dalam pemantauan kondisi zona perakaran pada lahan Spodosol yang memiliki keterbatasan fisik tanah.

Penelitian ini mendapatkan dukungan pendanaan dari **Universitas Gadjah Mada melalui Academic Excellence C Scheme 2025 No. 5719/UN1.P2/Dit-Lit/PT.01.03/2025**. Tim peneliti juga menyampaikan apresiasi kepada **Working Group Food Security (WG.FS 1.2) Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming, Pusat Unggulan Antar Perguruan Tinggi (PUAPT) Universitas Gadjah Mada**, atas dukungan fasilitas penelitian, serta kepada **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** atas dukungan teknis dan kelembagaan. Apresiasi juga disampaikan kepada **Nada Berliana Kusumawati, Iqbal Maulana Haryadi, Muhdan Syarovy, Suwardi, Sukarman, dan Septa Primananda** atas bantuan teknis dalam pengembangan sistem, pemasangan alat di lapangan, dan akuisisi data.

## **Manfaat dan Dampak:**

Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi penting bagi pengembangan **sistem monitoring tanah pada perkebunan kelapa sawit tropis**. Dengan pemantauan multikedalaman, pengelola kebun dapat memperoleh informasi yang lebih lengkap mengenai kondisi zona perakaran, bukan hanya kondisi tanah di permukaan. Informasi ini dapat membantu mendukung pengambilan keputusan terkait **irigasi, drainase, pengelolaan air, dan mitigasi stres tanaman**.

Sistem ini juga berpotensi membantu pengelola perkebunan dalam mengenali periode ketika zona perakaran berada pada kondisi **stabil, transisi, atau tidak stabil**. Dengan informasi tersebut, tindakan lapangan dapat dilakukan secara lebih tepat waktu dan berbasis data. Pendekatan ini penting terutama pada lahan dengan lapisan hardpan, karena kondisi air di permukaan belum tentu menggambarkan kondisi air pada lapisan tanah yang lebih dalam.

Dari sisi **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, penelitian ini mendukung **SDG 2: Zero Hunger** karena berkontribusi pada pengembangan teknologi untuk mendukung produktivitas dan keberlanjutan sistem pertanian. Penelitian ini juga sejalan dengan **SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation** melalui potensi pengelolaan air yang lebih efisien pada sistem perkebunan. Selain itu, pengembangan **sensor multikedalaman, sistem tertanam, dan indeks hidrotermal** mendukung **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure** melalui inovasi teknologi pertanian cerdas. Dalam jangka panjang, teknologi ini juga berkontribusi pada **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production** dan **SDG 13: Climate Action**, karena dapat membantu mendorong pengelolaan sumber daya air dan tanah secara lebih adaptif, efisien, dan berkelanjutan.

Ke depan, sistem ini berpotensi dikembangkan lebih lanjut melalui validasi pada berbagai **jenis tanah, kedalaman hardpan, kondisi drainase, tinggi muka air tanah, struktur kanopi**, serta **zona pengelolaan perkebunan yang berbeda**. Integrasi lebih lanjut dengan platform **Internet of Things (IoT), dashboard monitoring, sistem peringatan dini, dan model pengambilan keputusan** dapat memperkuat peran teknologi ini dalam mendukung manajemen air dan pemantauan stres hidrotermal pada perkebunan kelapa sawit tropis.

**Publikasi lengkap penelitian ini dapat diakses melalui tautan DOI berikut:**[https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2026.112026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2026.112026)
